summary: Structure, ontology terms, file coverage, sample/label map, fractions and the digest split all check out. But the instrument methods embedded in all 207 RAW files contradict two technical columns. comment[collision energy] says 32 NCE on every row, while all 100 rep2 files were acquired at NCE 35. comment[ms1 scan range] says 350-1550 m/z, while no file used that range: rep1 used 300-1700 and rep2 used 350-1700.

reviewer_context.context: Fresh subagent with no producer transcript. It read only the reviewer brief, the skill and contract, the artifact, the PXD015293 manifest, report and validation log, and the producer's PXD015293 evidence files (identity asserted). It re-fetched the PRIDE files/all list and the RAW headers itself. It did not read the earlier review-* dirs.

spec_compliance.evidence: sdrf-tools contract -t ms-proteomics@1.1.0 -t vertebrates@1.1.0: no required column is missing, and the only extra column is factor value[disease]. sdrf-tools structure exit 0. The reserved words are allowed by the allow_* flags. The (source name, assay name, label) key is unique, and so is the (source, bio rep, tech rep, fraction) coordinate. Modification syntax is OK, including PP=Protein N-term.

ontology_integrity.evidence: OLS4 resolved 19 unique terms. None is obsolete and every label matches: UBERON:0001891, MONDO:0005180, PATO:0000461, EFO:0001272, NCBITaxon:10090, MS:1001309, MS:1001910, MS:1000422, MS:1000484, PRIDE:0000564/0608/0599/0627/0325/0326, and UNIMOD:1/4/35/188. sdrf-tools check: 17/17 verified, 0 UNIMOD swaps.

source_evidence.evidence: Biological and sample-prep claims match the PMC8628316 full text (title verified), including the B6C3F2 embryos plus 'crossed to B6', C57BL/6J SILAM, LysC digests, DTT/IAA, 10 ppm/0.02 Da and Lys6. The instrument methods were read from the first 0.7-2 MB of all 207 RAW files, fetched from the PRIDE FTP. All 107 rep1 files use FTMS o(300.0-1700.0), HCD NCE 32.0, top 10 (acquired 2014). All 100 rep2 files use FTMS o(350.0-1700.0), HCD NCE 35.0, top 15 (acquired Jan 2016). The SDRF copies the paper prose (32 NCE, 350-1550), which the raw data contradicts.

file_mapping.evidence: A fresh PRIDE v3 files/all returned 320 entries, all with projectAccessions PXD015293, 303 of them RAW. The lysc SDRF has 207 unique files and the trypsin SDRF 96. They share no file, and their union equals the 303 RAW exactly. No Tryp file is in the lysc SDRF. Each file appears in exactly 2 rows (light and heavy). There are no peak lists.

design_consistency.evidence: The rows were recomputed from the file names. Arm maps to source name, disease, factor, strain and pooled status; label maps to the source; fraction equals the nominal number in the file name. All 414 rows match. The tech-rep rep+2n scheme is consistent and keeps the coordinate unique. Disease is PD for PFF and AAV1-tTA and normal for PBS and AAV1-GFP; the heavy reference has factor not applicable. The split by digest is justified: the A53T LysC flow-through and the Tryp retained digest are separately fractionated pools whose 1-24 fractions would collide.

omission_safety.evidence: Two technical values claim more than the evidence supports. The single 32 NCE value hides a two-method acquisition: rep2 used NCE 35 and top 15. The 350-1550 m/z range was not used by any run. No other unsupported specificity was found; sex = not available and midbrain are conservatively supported.

deterministic_validation.evidence: flock parse_sdrf validate-sdrf --sdrf_file <artifact> -t ms-proteomics -t vertebrates: 'only warnings', the 3 free-text strain values not being in NCBITaxon (expected). sdrf-tools check: CLEAN (exit 0). sdrf-tools score: 100/100 (exit 0). sdrf-tools structure: exit 0.

findings.message: Collision energy is 32 NCE, but all rep2 RAW files were acquired at HCD NCE 35.
findings.evidence: The embedded instrument methods of all 100 rep2 files (method 120m_120_30_8HCD_35_long_column_011216.meth, acquired in data dirs 011216/012716) show 'Normalized Coll. Energy: 35.0'. All 107 rep1 files show 32.0. The paper's 'HCD energy was set to 32 for mouse samples' is wrong for rep2. Example: Mouse_SILAM_PBS_rep2_F17b.raw and Mouse_SILAM_PFF_rep2_F24.raw.
findings.correction: Set 35 NCE on every rep2 row and keep 32 NCE on rep1. Cite the raw-header method in the manifest.

findings.message: The MS1 scan range is 350m/z-1550m/z, but no RAW file used that range.
findings.evidence: First scan event in the embedded method: rep1 (107 files) 'FTMS + p norm o(300.0-1700.0)', rep2 (100 files) 'o(350.0-1700.0)'. The paper's 'm/z 350-1550 ... top speed mode 3 s' does not match the Elite top-10/top-15 methods.
findings.correction: Use 300m/z-1700m/z on rep1 rows and 350m/z-1700m/z on rep2 rows, from the raw headers. Update the manifest claim.

findings.message: rep2 is a separate acquisition about 1.5 years later with a different method (top 15, NCE 35). This supports treating rep1/rep2 as technical series. Whether the suffixed files are re-injections is still undocumented, and the limitations already say so.
findings.evidence: Raw data dirs 110514/112214/040214 for rep1 and 011216/012716 for rep2.
findings.correction: Optionally add the method and date difference to the manifest limitation.

findings.message: The value 'B6C3F2 x C57BL/6 (B6C3F2 founders crossed to B6)' puts a parenthetical explanation inside the cell.
findings.evidence: The value is free text. The supporting text is in the manifest.
findings.correction: Optionally shorten it to 'B6C3F2 x C57BL/6'.

findings.message: The same method split probably affects the trypsin file's A53T rep1/rep2 Tryp rows.
findings.evidence: The LysC rows of the same mice and series use the 32/35 split.
findings.correction: Check the Tryp RAW headers and fix them the same way.
